cohorts.typical: Real-world pages at or near oracle parity. The median corpus page is AT parity, so a regression in the common case is invisible to the tail fixtures — these exist to catch it.
cohorts.tail-colour: Per-pixel colour conversion (PdfColorSpace.ToRgb), the previously known hotspot.
cohorts.tail-flat: Cost proportional to the INPUT, measured flat across 36/72/150 dpi. Work is being done in proportion to source data rather than to what the output needs.
cohorts.tail-scaling: Cost proportional to OUTPUT pixels — the normal shape with a bad constant.

provenance: Tail fixtures selected 2026-09-06 by mining renderMs against per-oracle timings in the corpus-scan reports, using *CachedRenderMs where an oracle hit the render cache and the MEDIAN oracle rather than the fastest. 55 of 4059 comparable pages (1.4%) are >=3x the median oracle and >=300 ms, and they account for 58.4% of excise's total render time. Do not compare against the fastest oracle or against an uncorrected cache hit: bug_2034 reads as 2462x that way and 14x fairly.
